To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glucose repression of invertasespecific mRNA is exerted at two different levels: (i) glucose regulates the amount of mRNA at the level transcription, and (ii) the expression of invertase mRNA present under repressive conditions is controlled by glucose at the translation and secretion levels.

1) glucose represses the synthesis and secretion of invertase at the level of mRNA translation and secretion, respectively; 2) this repression is due to a decrease in the affinity of the invertase message for the ribosome; 3) glucose repressors act at the same point as glucose, and 4) the repressor is a protein which binds to a region of the mRNA coding for invertase.
glucose regulates invertase synthesis at the level of mRNA synthesis, mRNA sensitivity and protein secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms by which the expression of invertase gene is regulated by the presence or absence of glucose in the medium.
the regulation of the expression of the invertasespecific messenger in S. cerevisae.
the study of the mechanisms of glucose repression in S. cerevisae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

glucose regulates the invertase gene by acting at three different levels: (i) at the level of gene expression; (ii) at the level translation; and (iii) at the level secretion (Mormenee & Sentandreu, 1984).
glucose represses the expression of invertase at the level of mRNA transcription and translation and by sensitization of mRNA to glucose.
glucose regulates the synthesis of invertase at the level of mRNA formation and that glucose also regulates the translation and/or secretion of the invertase messenger RNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
glucose regulates the concentration of the invertase-specific mRNA at the level at which it is synthesized, as well as its translation and secretion.
glucose regulates the concentration of invertase-specific mRNA by controlling its transcription rate.

the glucose repression of invertases in S. cerevisia e involves the regulation of the expression of invertase mRNA at the transcriptional and translational levels, as well as the regulation of the synthesis of invertase at the post-translational level (Mormene & Sentandreu, 1984).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of a single gene, such as the invertase gene, can be regulated at different levels.
the glucose repression of invertases is mediated at the level of mRNA and that this regulation is a complex phenomenon involving the synthesis, translation, and secretion of the protein.

there is an important role for the hexose in regulating the expression of the mRNA for this enzyme and that the regulation occurs at the level of both transcription and translation (Mormeneosentandreu 1983).
